cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic hand-woven strip cloth in the distinctive Kente pattern—colorful geometric blocks in blue, yellow, red, green, and black arranged in the traditional strip-woven format characteristic of Ashanti (and Ewe) textile production in Ghana.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, composed of 4 strips of rayon (or possibly silk), hand-woven and hand sewn together along the selvedges. The warp is of yellow, maroon and black threads forming four narrow stripes against a blue background. A weft chequerboard pattern has been formed along the central area of the cloth using green, black, maroon, and white thread and a second pair of heedles to weave two solid two blocks of colour that flank geometric patterns in discontinuous supplementary weft in yellow and maroon. At both ends of the cloth is a variant pattern with six bands of design running across all four strips. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
